source.citation: Census Bureau, 2023 County Business Patterns, county file, March employment by two-digit NAICS sector (private employers). BLS OEWS May 2025 state ownership research estimates: federal, state and local government, including schools and hospitals. BLS notes these carry more model error than standard estimates. BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025: area, state and national tables, 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentile annual wage, all ownerships. Existing Census County Business Patterns 2023 county sector employment and BLS OEWS May 2025 public ownership mix in src/core2/reference/town-employment.generated.ts; not resident employment or observed establishment staff.; Existing TOWN_WORKPLACES and Role weights in town-employment.ts are authored game assumptions, not measured sector-to-SOC staffing shares.; Existing TOWN_JOB_SOC and BLS OEWS May 2025 wage references in town-pay.generated.ts; same-occupation national median is a labeled fallback where no local observation exists.; Existing BLS Employee Tenure in January 2026 age-cohort median table in town-employment.ts; later-vintage opening proxy, no individual tenure spread reconstructed. U.S. Census Bureau, 2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B23001 (Sex by Age by Employment Status for the Population 16 Years and Over), table-based summary file https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/acsdt5y2024-b23001.dat, county rows (summary level 050), with Puerto Rico's municipios. Each age row pools the male and female cells; the civilian population is the pooled total minus the table's armed-forces subtotal, and 65-and-over rows (which have no armed-forces branch) carry the age total.
source.estimatedFrom: Population-scaled finite opening allocation over recorded employers and already recorded compatible employee roles. Initial seed order distributes who held opening positions among supported real options; it never selects a future application, hire, firing or desired biography. Unsupported reference weight stays omitted. Role template work-role_053f3a95079db36a, employer organization_564ac4ec5c68fe6e; cohort target 245 for restaurant:service:food-server:Server. SOC 35-3031, area 48300, percentile 71.06215332695282. Hours retain the recorded role estimate. BLS age-band median tenure, spread within the band (an exponential at that median, the worker's place in it a generation fact), bounded by adulthood and by an employer founding recorded before the opening; start 2001-03-17. Initial generated assignment, not an application, offered vacancy, acceptance or future hiring decision.

personality-v1:facet-acquisitive.estimatedFrom: ESTIMATED FROM RECORDS AND PUBLIC DATA: available parents, household adults, payroll, place and congregation records are used first. Missing sibling counts use the national U.S. Census SIPP 2009 distribution and missing pay bands use ACS 2024 B17024; both are labeled estimates and sampled by the person's stable generation key. Caregiver availability uses recorded adults or a saved family pattern's parents per child. Cohort scope: exact; exact place/type/income first, same place next, then the game's recorded families. Current payroll takes priority; otherwise the existing BLS May 2025 place/occupation wage reader and recorded job tenure/hours supply a labeled pay proxy. Income contributors are retained in incomeSourcePersonIds. No relative, emotional treatment, faith or event is created. ESTIMATED FROM RECORDS AND NATIONAL DATA: siblings, congregation, household pay, caregivers per child, school-year moves and a parent's death are weighed smoothly; missing sibling counts use sipp-2009-p70-126-table-4, and missing pay bands use acs-2024-1yr-b17024-adolescence. ESTIMATED FROM THE NATIONAL DISTRIBUTION: no household pay is recorded for this childhood period, so a stable sample for this person uses the ACS 2024 1-year B17024 U.S. child distribution for early-childhood. ESTIMATED FROM THE NATIONAL DISTRIBUTION: no household pay is recorded for this childhood period, so a stable sample for this person uses the ACS 2024 1-year B17024 U.S. child distribution for adolescence. Canonical sparse upbringing trait projection; no traits inferred from names or gender.
